verses.zh: （ 亞 薩 的 詩 ， 交 與 伶 長 。 調 用 為 證 的 百 合 花 。 ） 領 約 瑟 如 領 羊 群 之 以 色 列 的 牧 者 啊 ， 求 你 留 心 聽 ！ 坐 在 二 基 路 伯 上 的 啊 ， 求 你 發 出 光 來 ！
verses.en: For the music director, according to the shushan-eduth style;[NOTE:1] a psalm of Asaph.O Shepherd of Israel, pay attention,you who lead Joseph like a flock of sheep.You who sit enthroned above the cherubim,[NOTE:2] reveal your splendor.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 80. The psalmist laments Israel’s demise and asks the Lord to show favor toward his people, as he did in earlier times.
The Hebrew expression shushan-eduth means “lily of the testimony.” It may refer to a particular music style or to a tune title. See the superscription to Ps 60.

Cherubim are winged angels. As depicted in the OT, they possess both human and animal (lion, ox, and eagle) characteristics (see Ezek 1:10; 10:14, 21; 41:18). They are pictured as winged creatures (Exod 25:20; 37:9; 1 Kgs 6:24-27; Ezek 10:8, 19) and serve as the very throne of God when the ark of the covenant is in view (Ps 99:1; see Num 7:89; 1 Sam 4:4; 2 Sam 6:2; 2 Kgs 19:15). The picture of the Lord seated on the cherubim suggests they might be used by him as a vehicle, a function they carry out in Ezek 1:22-28 (the “living creatures” mentioned here are identified as cherubim in Ezek 10:20). In Ps 18:10 the image of a cherub serves to personify the wind.

verses.zh: 在 以 法 蓮 、 便 雅 憫 、 瑪 拿 西 前 面 施 展 你 的 大 能 ， 來 救 我 們 。
verses.en: In the sight of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh reveal[NOTE:1] your power.Come and deliver us.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “shine forth.”sn Reveal your splendor. The psalmist may allude to Deut 33:2, where God “shines forth” from Sinai and comes to superintend Moses’ blessing of the tribes.
Heb “stir up”; “arouse.”

verses.zh: 神 啊 ， 求 你 使 我 們 回 轉 （ 或 譯 ： 復 興 ） ， 使 你 的 臉 發 光 ， 我 們 便 要 得 救 ！
verses.en: O God, restore us.Smile on us.[NOTE:1] Then we will be delivered.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “come for our deliverance.”
The idiom “cause your face to shine” probably refers to a smile (see Eccl 8:1), which in turn suggests favor and blessing (see Num 6:25; Pss 4:6; 31:16; 44:3; 67:1; 89:15; Dan 9:17).

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 ─ 萬 軍 之 神 啊 ， 你 向 你 百 姓 的 禱 告 發 怒 ， 要 到 幾 時 呢 ？
verses.en: O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] how long will you remain angry at your people while they pray to you?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cause your face to shine in order that we may be delivered.” After the imperative, the cohortative with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose/result.

Heb “Lord, God, hosts.” One expects the construct form אֱלֹהֵי (ʾelohe) before צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot; “hosts”; see Ps 89:9), but יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (yehvah ʾelohim) precedes צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot) in Pss 59:5 and 84:8 as well. In this context the term “hosts” has been rendered “Heaven’s Armies.”

verses.zh: 你 以 眼 淚 當 食 物 給 他 們 吃 ， 又 多 量 出 眼 淚 給 他 們 喝 。
verses.en: You have given them tears as food;[NOTE:1] you have made them drink tears by the measure.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “How long will you remain angry during the prayer of your people.” Some take the preposition ב (bet) in an adversative sense here (“at/against the prayer of your people”), but the temporal sense is preferable. The psalmist expects persistent prayer to pacify God.
Heb “you have fed them the food of tears.”

verses.zh: 你 使 鄰 邦 因 我 們 紛 爭 ； 我 們 的 仇 敵 彼 此 戲 笑 。
verses.en: You have made our neighbors dislike us[NOTE:1] and our enemies insult us.
notes: Heb “[by] the third part [of a measure].” The Hebrew term שָׁלִישׁ (shalish, “third part [of a measure]”) occurs only here and in Isa 40:12.

verses.zh: 萬 軍 之 神 啊 ， 求 你 使 我 們 回 轉 ， 使 你 的 臉 發 光 ， 我 們 便 要 得 救 ！
verses.en: O God of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] restore us.Smile on us.[NOTE:2] Then we will be delivered.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you have made us an object of contention to our neighbors.”

Heb “O God, hosts.” One expects the construct form אֱלֹהֵי before צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot, “hosts”; see Ps 89:9), but יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (yehvah ʾelohim) precedes צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot) in Pss 59:5 and 84:8 as well. See also v. 4 for a similar construction.
The idiom “cause your face to shine” probably refers to a smile (see Eccl 8:1), which in turn suggests favor and blessing (see Num 6:25; Pss 4:6; 31:16; 44:3; 67:1; 89:15; Dan 9:17).

verses.zh: 你 從 埃 及 挪 出 一 棵 葡 萄 樹 ， 趕 出 外 邦 人 ， 把 這 樹 栽 上 。
verses.en: You uprooted a vine[NOTE:1] from Egypt;you drove out nations and transplanted it.
notes: Heb “cause your face to shine in order that we may be delivered.” After the imperative, the cohortative with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose/result.

verses.zh: 你 在 這 樹 根 前 預 備 了 地 方 ， 他 就 深 深 扎 根 ， 爬 滿 了 地 。
verses.en: You cleared the ground for it;[NOTE:1] it took root[NOTE:2] and filled the land.
notes: The vine is here a metaphor for Israel (see Ezek 17:6-10; Hos 10:1).
Heb “you cleared away before it.”

verses.zh: 他 的 影 子 遮 滿 了 山 ， 枝 子 好 像 佳 美 的 香 柏 樹 。
verses.en: The mountains were covered by its shadow,the highest cedars[NOTE:1] by its branches.
notes: Heb “and it took root [with] its roots.”

verses.zh: 他 發 出 枝 子 ， 長 到 大 海 ， 發 出 蔓 子 ， 延 到 大 河 。
verses.en: Its branches reached the Mediterranean Sea,[NOTE:1] and its shoots the Euphrates River.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cedars of God.” The divine name אֵל (ʾel, “God”) is here used in an idiomatic manner to indicate the superlative.
Heb “to [the] sea.” The “sea” refers here to the Mediterranean Sea.

verses.zh: 你 為 何 拆 毀 這 樹 的 籬 笆 ， 任 憑 一 切 過 路 的 人 摘 取 ？
verses.en: Why did you break down its walls,[NOTE:1] so that all who pass by pluck its fruit?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to [the] river.” The “river” is the Euphrates River in Mesopotamia. Israel expanded both to the west and to the east.
The protective walls of the metaphorical vineyard are in view here (see Isa 5:5).

verses.zh: 林 中 出 來 的 野 豬 把 他 糟 踏 ； 野 地 的 走 獸 拿 他 當 食 物 。
verses.en: The wild boars of the forest ruin it;[NOTE:1] the insects[NOTE:2] of the field feed on it.
notes: Heb “pluck it.”
The Hebrew verb כִּרְסֵם (kirsem, “to eat away; to ruin”) occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 萬 軍 之 神 啊 ， 求 你 回 轉 ！ 從 天 上 垂 看 ， 眷 顧 這 葡 萄 樹 ，
verses.en: O God of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] come back.Look down from heaven and take notice.Take care of this vine,
notes: The precise referent of the Hebrew word translated “insects,” which occurs only here and in Ps 50:11, is uncertain. Aramaic, Arabic, and Akkadian cognates refer to insects, such as locusts or crickets.

verses.zh: 保 護 你 右 手 所 栽 的 和 你 為 自 已 所 堅 固 的 枝 子 。
verses.en: the root[NOTE:1] your right hand planted,the shoot you made to grow.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “O God, hosts.” One expects the construct form אֱלֹהֵי before צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot, “hosts”; see Ps 89:9), but יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (yehvah ʾelohim) precedes צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot) in Pss 59:5 and 84:8 as well. See also vv. 4, 7 for a similar construction.

The form וְכַנָּה (vekhannah, “and a root”) is understood as וְכַנָּהּ (vekhannah), taking the ה (he) at the end as the third feminine singular pronominal suffix הּ (he with mappiq is hard “h”) rather than as the noun ending (see HALOT 483 s.v. III כֵּן). Elsewhere the noun refers to a pedestal or base, most often for the wash basin between the tabernacle and the altar. Translations here vary as “root” (NIV), “shoot” (NASB), “stock” (ASV, ESV, RSV), or the contextually driven “vineyard” (KJV).

verses.zh: 這 樹 已 經 被 火 焚 燒 ， 被 刀 砍 伐 ； 他 們 因 你 臉 上 的 怒 容 就 滅 亡 了 。
verses.en: It is burned[NOTE:1] and cut down.May those who did this die because you are displeased with them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and upon a son you strengthened for yourself.” In this context, where the extended metaphor of the vine dominates, בֵּן (ben, “son”) probably refers to the shoots that grow from the vine. Cf. Gen 49:22.
Heb “burned with fire.”

verses.zh: 願 你 的 手 扶 持 你 右 邊 的 人 ， 就 是 你 為 自 已 所 堅 固 的 人 子 。
verses.en: May you give support to the one you have chosen,[NOTE:1] to the one whom you raised up for yourself.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “because of the rebuke of your face they perish.”

Heb “may your hand be upon the man of your right hand.” The referent of the otherwise unattested phrase “man of your right hand,” is unclear. It may refer to the nation collectively as a man. (See the note on the word “yourself” in v. 17b.)

verses.zh: 這 樣 ， 我 們 便 不 退 後 離 開 你 ； 求 你 救 活 我 們 ， 我 們 就 要 求 告 你 的 名 。
verses.en: Then we will not turn away from you.Revive us and we will pray to you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “upon the son of man you strengthened for yourself.” In its only other use in the Book of Psalms, the phrase “son of man” refers to the human race in general (see Ps 8:4). Here the phrase may refer to the nation collectively as a man. Note the use of the statement “you strengthened for yourself” both here and in v. 15, where the “son” (i.e., the branch of the vine) refers to Israel.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 ─ 萬 軍 之 神 啊 ， 求 你 使 我 們 回 轉 ， 使 你 的 臉 發 光 ， 我 們 便 要 得 救 ！
verses.en: O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] restore us.Smile on us.[NOTE:2] Then we will be delivered.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and in your name we will call.”

Heb “O Lord, God, hosts.” One expects the construct form אֱלֹהֵי before צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot, “hosts”; see Ps 89:9), but יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (yehvah ʾelohim) precedes צְבָאוֹת (tsevaʾot) in Pss 59:5 and 84:8 as well. See also vv. 4, 7, 14 for a similar construction.
The idiom “cause your face to shine” probably refers to a smile (see Eccl 8:1), which in turn suggests favor and blessing (see Num 6:25; Pss 4:6; 31:16; 44:3; 67:1; 89:15; Dan 9:17).
